hero.headline: Trump names housing official Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, as acting director of national intelligence, days after Tulsi Gabbard's departure from the role. Pulte, an heir to the PulteGroup home construction fortune, has no known background in national security or intelligence work.

Trump announced the decision on his Truth Social platform, saying "William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America." Pulte will retain his position leading the FHFA, which oversees federal housing lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

The appointment has generated significant concern among Republicans and observers. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters that the intelligence community needs "professionals" and cautioned that Pulte would face "a lengthy road ahead" if Trump nominated him for permanent confirmation. "We don't need a weaponized" national intelligence director, Thune said, noting that any permanent appointment would require Senate approval and extensive hearings.

Pulte's tenure at the FHFA has drawn scrutiny. Since taking the role, he has used the agency to level allegations against Trump's political opponents, including accusing Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud. Cook has denied wrongdoing. A former high-ranking official described his handling of the Cook case as "very bizarre."

Critics have highlighted Pulte's lack of government experience before joining the Trump administration. Upon arriving at the FHFA, he fired members of the boards of both Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and appointed himself as chair. The New York Times reported that Pulte no longer holds any official connection to PulteGroup, having been removed from the company's board in 2020.

His family has also distanced itself from him. The Pulte Family Charitable Foundation issued a statement in 2023 saying that Pulte "is not a representative of, nor has he served in any capacity" for the organization, and that some of his public communications "may have created confusion" with the family's charitable endeavors.

Gabbard's exit from the intelligence director role came after a turbulent tenure marked by being largely sidelined during Trump's military operations and foreign policy decisions. Trump had been asking cabinet members as early as April about replacing her, according to people briefed on internal discussions.

The position of director of national intelligence coordinates intelligence gathering across federal agencies including the CIA and NSA. The role was created after the September 11 attacks to improve communication between intelligence agencies. The acting designation allows Pulte to serve without Senate confirmation for a limited period, though any permanent appointment would require approval from the Senate intelligence committee and full chamber confirmation.

cards.headline: Israel Continues Strikes as Lebanon Peace Talks Resume in Washington
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue operations against Hezbollah even as Lebanese and Israeli officials met for negotiations.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue military operations against Hezbollah while Lebanese and Israeli officials held talks in Washington. Israel has maintained its campaign in southern Lebanon, though it has not struck Beirut following a US-announced deal.

The negotiations proceeded as Iran halted discussions with the U.S., citing Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza. Trump stated that Israel and Hezbollah would cease fighting once Iran resumed talks with the United States.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes on Ukrainian Cities Kill at Least 22
cards.body:
Russia launched a massive overnight assault using hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles against multiple Ukrainian cities, killing at least 22 people and trapping others beneath collapsed buildings. The coordinated attack targeted Kyiv and other major population centers across the country.

According to Ukraine's air force, Russia fired 73 missiles and 656 drones in the overnight strikes. The weapons included eight hypersonic Tsirkon missiles. The main targets were Kyiv, the central cities of Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, and the eastern cities of Poltava and Kharkiv.

In Dnipro, the strikes proved particularly devastating, with at least five people killed in that city alone. Local authorities reported that four bodies were found in the ruins of a destroyed house, and workers continued searching for survivors on Saturday morning. The attacks caused fires to break out across Dnipro and partly destroyed several apartment blocks, businesses, and a private house. Another person was killed in a separate strike in the region on Saturday afternoon. Overall, at least 34 people were injured across the strikes.

Odesa and Kharkiv were also targeted by drones, with at least three people injured in those cities. Ukrainian air defense officials said they repelled most of the more than 600 Russian drones launched during the assault, which appears to have been the largest attack in several days.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the Russian tactics on social media, noting that the strikes focused on civilian infrastructure. "Most of the targets are ordinary infrastructure in cities," Zelenskyy wrote. "Residential buildings, energy, and enterprises have been damaged."

The overnight assault followed a prisoner exchange on Friday, in which Russia and Ukraine exchanged 193 service members. That exchange was one outcome of US-brokered negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv, though the talks have made no progress on key issues that would end Russia's invasion.

In response to the strikes, Zelenskyy asked US President Donald Trump to send Patriot missiles to Ukraine to help defend against future attacks.

Ukraine also carried out some of its longest-distance drone strikes deep inside Russian territory during the same period. In Russia's border region of Belgorod, a woman was killed and a man seriously injured by a Ukrainian drone strike.

Ukrainian authorities continued to assess the full extent of the damage and casualties from the overnight attack. Emergency services worked to clear debris and search for survivors in affected areas across multiple cities.

cards.headline: Trump signs order seeking voluntary AI safety reviews before public release
cards.teaser: The president signed an executive order asking artificial intelligence companies to submit their most powerful models for government testing.
cards.body:
Trump signed an executive order establishing a voluntary framework for federal review of advanced AI models before public release. Under the guidelines, tech companies would submit their most powerful AI systems to the government for testing up to 30 days prior to launching them publicly.

The administration frames the initiative as a national security measure, particularly regarding cybersecurity threats. The voluntary nature of the framework reflects Trump's reluctance to impose mandatory regulations on the tech industry, despite his stated concerns about AI-related security risks.

cards.headline: Canada Requests 16-Year Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc wrote to US and Mexican counterparts proposing renewal of the USMCA agreement.
cards.body:
Canada has formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade deal. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc sent letters to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico proposing the extension of the North American free trade agreement.

The renewal would extend the current trade framework governing commerce between the three nations for more than a decade and a half.

cards.headline: California voters cast ballots in competitive primary races for governor and Los Angeles mayor
cards.teaser: Voters across California are selecting party nominees for governor and deciding local races including Los Angeles mayor.
cards.body:
California held primary elections on June 2 with competitive races for governor and Los Angeles mayor. Voters across the state cast ballots to determine party nominees who will advance to the general election.

The Democratic gubernatorial primary drew significant attention and spending. Tech billionaires invested hundreds of millions of dollars in California races ahead of the primary, with Google co-founder Sergey Brin alone spending $82 million since January, primarily to oppose a billionaire tax on the November ballot. Democratic gubernatorial candidate Matt Mahan received more donations than any other candidate.

cards.headline: Sanders to propose giving public 50 percent ownership of large AI companies
cards.teaser: Senator Bernie Sanders plans to introduce legislation that would grant the public a 50 percent stake in major artificial intelligence companies.
cards.body:
Sanders announced in a video message that he will introduce the AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act in the coming weeks. The Vermont independent said the bill would give the American public a 50 percent ownership stake in large AI companies.

The senator delivered his announcement in a nearly seven-minute video on the proposal. Sanders has been a vocal advocate for government intervention in technology and corporate sectors throughout his career in the Senate.

cards.headline: Four Migrant Farm Workers Killed in Italy Minivan Fire, Two Arrested
cards.teaser: Authorities arrested two people after security footage showed them blocking a van's doors and throwing liquid inside to start a fire.
cards.body:
Two people have been arrested following a fatal fire at a minivan in Italy that killed four migrant farm workers. CCTV footage showed the suspects blocking the van's doors from outside and throwing liquid inside before setting the fire alight.

The four agricultural workers were unable to escape the vehicle and died in the blaze. Police used security camera evidence to identify and apprehend the two suspects responsible for the attack.

cards.headline: British Police Face Scrutiny After Handcuffing Dying Stabbing Victim
cards.teaser: Authorities are investigating officers who handcuffed student Henry Nowak while he was dying from a stab wound in a case fueling outrage.
cards.body:
British police are under investigation for handcuffing student Henry Nowak while he was dying from a stab wound. The case has sparked widespread outrage and become a flashpoint for debate over policing practices and race relations in the UK.

Three officers who arrested Nowak remain on front-line duty as the investigation continues. Police officials have condemned calls for vigilante justice in response to the murder. The case has drawn political attention as authorities examine the circumstances surrounding the officers' actions during the incident.

cards.headline: Israel Continues Strikes as Lebanon Peace Talks Resume in Washington
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue operations against Hezbollah even as Lebanese and Israeli officials met for negotiations.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue military operations against Hezbollah while Lebanese and Israeli officials held talks in Washington. Israel has maintained its campaign in southern Lebanon, though it has not struck Beirut following a US-announced deal.

The negotiations proceeded as Iran halted discussions with the U.S., citing Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza. Trump stated that Israel and Hezbollah would cease fighting once Iran resumed talks with the United States.

cards.headline: Protests Intensify in Albania Over Kushner-Linked Resort Development
cards.teaser: Plans for luxury resorts on the Adriatic Sea have become a flashpoint for broader frustrations with the government.
cards.body:
Demonstrations are growing in Albania over plans for luxury resort developments on the Adriatic Sea with ties to Kushner. The projects have long worried environmentalists concerned about coastal preservation and environmental impact.

The resort plans have evolved into a broader symbol of public dissatisfaction with the Albanian government. Protesters are using the development controversy as a rallying point for wider grievances about governance and policy decisions affecting the country.

cards.headline: White House Correspondents' Dinner Rescheduled After Shooting
cards.teaser: The annual dinner was interrupted when a gunman stormed a security checkpoint in April.
cards.body:
The White House Correspondents' Dinner, held annually in April, was interrupted when a gunman stormed a security checkpoint during the event. President Trump was swiftly evacuated from the gala following the incident on April 25.

Organizers have rescheduled the dinner for July 24. Trump has confirmed his attendance at the summer event.

cards.headline: Canada Requests 16-Year Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc wrote to US and Mexican counterparts proposing renewal of the USMCA agreement.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Trump administration plans to shelve controversial Justice Department fund amid Republican criticism
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is backing away from a Justice Department fund that drew bipartisan concern over potential misuse.
cards.body:
The Trump administration will comply with a court ruling that halted a $1.8 billion Justice Department fund. The Justice Department said it "disagrees strongly" with the decision to stop the fund's establishment.

House Speaker Mike Johnson announced plans to shelve the fund after Republican lawmakers raised concerns about its purpose and oversight. Republicans worried it could operate as a slush fund without proper congressional control. Trump officials met with lawmakers to address the controversy before deciding to abandon the initiative.

cards.teaser: Voters across California are selecting party nominees for governor and deciding local races including Los Angeles mayor.

cards.headline: Kenyan court extends block on U.S. Ebola treatment facility
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court extended an order blocking the United States from establishing a hospital for American Ebola patients in Kenya.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has extended its order preventing the establishment of a U.S. facility designed to treat American citizens with Ebola. The decision marks another obstacle to the U.S. government's effort to create a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya.

The proposed facility has faced significant pushback from Kenyan citizens and civil society groups, who have organized protests against the project. The court also instructed the Kenyan government to disclose information about the planned treatment center.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Representative Tom Kean Jr., who has been absent from Congress
cards.teaser: The president endorsed a New Jersey congressman who has been missing from Washington for nearly three months.
cards.body:
Trump endorsed Representative Tom Kean Jr. in New Jersey's Republican primary despite the congressman's absence from Congress since early March. Kean cast his last House floor vote on March 5 and has been out due to a health issue. He is running unopposed in Tuesday's Republican primary.

Meanwhile, the Democratic primary in the seventh district has attracted multiple candidates and significant fundraising. Democrats are preparing their campaign strategy ahead of the general election.

cards.headline: White House Correspondents' Dinner rescheduled after shooting disrupted event
cards.teaser: The annual dinner for White House journalists will be held on July 24 after a shooting forced organizers to cancel the original event.
cards.body:
The White House Correspondents' Association rescheduled its annual dinner for July 24 after a shooting incident disrupted the original April event. A gunman stormed a security checkpoint at the Washington gala on April 25, forcing the cancellation of the formal dinner that typically brings together journalists, administration officials, and media figures.

President Trump was swiftly evacuated from the venue during the incident. He has confirmed his attendance at the rescheduled summer event, pledging to participate in the gala despite the disruption to the original spring gathering.

hero.headline: SpaceX Targets $1.75 Trillion Valuation in Record IPO
hero.body:
SpaceX has acquired Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI in a transformative merger that could reshape the aerospace and AI sectors. The deal, valued at $1.25 trillion combined, consolidates major parts of Musk's business empire ahead of a planned public offering expected in early summer.

The merger brings together SpaceX's rocket launch operations and satellite internet service Starlink with xAI's artificial intelligence technology, including the Grok chatbot and the social media platform X. In a joint statement, the companies described the combined entity as "the most ambitious, vertically-integrated innovation engine on (and off) Earth, with AI, rockets, space-based internet, direct-to-mobile device communications and the world's foremost real-time information and free speech platform."

The deal reportedly values SpaceX at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion. The combined business is on track for a stock market listing that would exceed $1 trillion in valuation, positioning it as one of the largest IPOs ever.

The merger announcement cited space-based artificial intelligence infrastructure as a key strategic rationale. The companies stated that current AI advancement depends on massive terrestrial datacenters requiring enormous amounts of power and cooling. They argued that global electricity demand for AI cannot be met through ground-based solutions without causing hardship to communities and the environment. "In the long term, space-based AI is obviously the only way to scale," the announcement said.

Musk has pursued plans to deploy datacenters and solar-powered satellites in space to power artificial intelligence systems, an undertaking of significant technical and financial complexity.

SpaceX has experienced dramatic valuation growth in recent years. The company sent a letter to investors in December revealing an expected valuation of $800 billion, based on its dominance in satellite launches and extensive contracts with the U.S. federal government.

xAI has similarly expanded its valuation amid the artificial intelligence investment boom. The company announced a $20 billion Series E funding round last month from major investors, valuing it at $230 billion.

The IPO is expected to occur in early summer, with speculation that the timing could coincide with a planetary alignment and Musk's birthday in late June.

This consolidation represents Musk's broader strategy of integrating his various business ventures. Earlier in 2025, xAI acquired the platform X in an all-stock transaction. Tesla also revealed plans to invest $2 billion in xAI last month.

The news provides a positive development for Musk following recent challenges. Tesla released an earnings report showing declining revenues and weakness in its automobile business, and Musk has faced scrutiny following the Department of Justice's release of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein.

cards.headline: Container Ship Struck by Projectiles in Iraqi Port
cards.teaser: Two projectiles hit a vessel owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company at an Iraqi port, highlighting threats to commercial shipping.
cards.body:
A ship owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company was struck by two projectiles while in an Iraqi port. The attack occurred as the United States and Iran work on negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments.

The incident underscores ongoing risks to commercial vessels operating in the region. Mediterranean Shipping Company is one of the world's largest container shipping firms, operating hundreds of vessels on routes connecting Asia, Europe, and the Middle East.

cards.headline: Six States Sue Trump Administration Over Offshore Wind Deal
cards.teaser: A group of states filed a lawsuit challenging a Trump administration agreement that paid a French company $1 billion to cancel wind farm projects.
cards.body:
Six state attorneys general sued the Trump administration on Tuesday over a deal to cancel a major offshore wind lease off New York's coast. In March, federal officials announced they would pay nearly $1 billion in taxpayer dollars to French energy company TotalEnergies to terminate plans for two offshore windfarms off New York and North Carolina.

Under the agreement, TotalEnergies pledged to abandon the projects and commit not to develop any new offshore wind projects in the United States. In exchange, the company will invest hundreds of millions of dollars in oil and gas projects instead. The states argue the deal is unlawful.

cards.headline: Alphabet Plans to Raise $80 Billion in Stock Sales for AI Investments
cards.teaser: Google's parent company announced plans to raise $80 billion through stock offerings to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion.
cards.body:
Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion through equity sales to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion. The fundraising effort is the largest equity offering on record, exceeding the combined proceeds of the three biggest IPOs ever. Berkshire Hathaway is participating with a $10 billion investment in the stock sale.

The massive capital raise underscores the substantial investment demands of AI development and infrastructure buildout. The move highlights how publicly traded tech companies are leveraging equity markets to finance the rapid expansion of AI capabilities and data center operations required to compete in the emerging AI economy.

cards.headline: Stephen Curry Signs Deal With Chinese Sneaker Company Li-Ning
cards.teaser: The NBA star agreed to a partnership with Li-Ning covering sportswear, athleisure products, and retail stores in the US and China.
cards.body:
Stephen Curry reached an agreement with Chinese athletic brand Li-Ning in what represents the largest deal between an NBA player and a Chinese company. The partnership will include sneakers, sportswear, and athleisure lines. Plans call for opening retail stores in both the United States and China.

The deal marks a shift in the business relationship between American basketball stars and Chinese brands. Li-Ning has previously signed smaller contracts with NBA players but none approaching this scale. Curry had been associated with Under Armour for years before this new partnership.

cards.headline: Martin Scorsese Backs AI Image Generation Startup
cards.teaser: The director invested in Black Forest Labs, signaling Hollywood's changing attitude toward artificial intelligence tools.
cards.body:
Martin Scorsese has backed Black Forest Labs, an artificial intelligence startup that develops image and video generation tools. His investment signals a shift in Hollywood's traditionally cautious stance toward AI technology, which the industry has long viewed with concern over job displacement and creative control.

Scorsese is using the technology specifically for storyboarding, positioning him as an unlikely but prominent advocate for AI tools among established filmmakers. His involvement suggests growing acceptance of AI applications in film production.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Sales Rebound With Gen Z Shoppers
cards.teaser: The lingerie retailer reported renewed success with younger customers after changes to its marketing approach and pricing strategy.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret has regained popularity among Gen Z consumers following strategic changes by its CEO. The company moved away from constant promotional sales cycles and adjusted its marketing approach. The shift has improved the retailer's financial performance and stock price.

The turnaround follows years of declining relevance for the brand among younger shoppers. Victoria's Secret focused on improving its core products, particularly bras, according to market analysts. The company's stock rose sharply on the news, heading toward its best single-day performance on record.

hero.headline: Microsoft launches Scout AI assistant for workplace tasks
hero.body:
Microsoft introduced Scout, a new artificial intelligence assistant designed to operate within the Microsoft 365 system. The company unveiled the product at its Build conference, positioning it as a personal agent that remains continuously active.

Scout draws inspiration from OpenClaw, an existing AI framework, and aims to bring similar capabilities into Microsoft's workplace software ecosystem. The assistant represents Microsoft's attempt to integrate AI-powered task management directly into the tools used by office workers daily.

Microsoft described Scout as the first genuine personal assistant the company has offered to customers. The tool functions as an AI coworker designed to handle tasks without requiring constant user supervision. The assistant runs persistently within the Microsoft 365 environment, allowing it to manage ongoing work processes.

The launch comes as major technology companies compete to embed AI assistants into productivity software. Microsoft has been integrating various AI features across its product lineup, with Scout representing a broader push toward autonomous AI agents that can operate with minimal human intervention.

Microsoft also released a homegrown reasoning model alongside Scout, expanding the company's portfolio of AI technologies. The assistant is meant to function like an executive assistant, handling scheduling, coordination, and other administrative tasks that typically require human attention.

cards.headline: Google adds deepfake call detection to Android phones
cards.teaser: Google introduced technology to identify scam calls that use AI-generated voices to impersonate trusted contacts.
cards.body:
Google rolled out new scam detection features for Android devices in its June update. The technology identifies calls where scammers use AI deepfake voices to impersonate authority figures, family members, or employers. The system also detects when callers spoof trusted phone numbers to make fraudulent calls appear legitimate.

The feature addresses a shift in scammer tactics as more people refuse to answer calls from unknown numbers. Google's Phone app will alert users when it detects potential impersonation attempts. The June Android update also includes expanded AirDrop device support and additional AI features.

cards.headline: Uber limits employee AI spending after budget depletes in four months
cards.teaser: The ride-hailing company imposed spending caps after staff consumed AI tool budgets faster than anticipated.
cards.body:
Uber has capped employee access to artificial intelligence tools after rapidly exhausting its allocated budget in just four months. The restriction marks a sharp reversal from the company's earlier stance, when it had actively encouraged workers to use AI extensively in their roles.

The swift depletion of funds underscores how quickly employees adopted AI tools once given access, outpacing what company leadership had anticipated. The move reflects the broader challenge companies face as they attempt to scale AI adoption while managing its substantial costs.

cards.headline: Microsoft releases open-source testing framework for AI systems
cards.teaser: The company introduced a tool that lets developers create AI behavior tests using plain text descriptions.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for Evaluation and Regression Testing, an open-source framework that streamlines how developers test AI systems. Rather than writing traditional code-based test suites, developers can now define AI behavior tests using text-based specifications.

The framework enables developer, compliance, and security teams to establish policies that AI agents must follow. These policies are stored in portable files that function across different platforms, giving organizations better control over AI agent behavior as these systems become increasingly autonomous.

cards.headline: Everand bundles e-books and audiobooks to compete with Amazon
cards.teaser: The startup combined reading formats and book club features in a single subscription service.
cards.body:
Everand launched a new subscription service that combines e-books, audiobooks, and book club features from its partner platform Fable. The bundled offering positions itself as a competitor to Amazon's separate Kindle and Audible services.

By integrating multiple formats and community features into one subscription, Everand gives readers access to different content types and social reading experiences without juggling separate accounts and services.

cards.headline: Martin Scorsese endorses AI for film storyboarding
cards.teaser: The director became an unexpected Hollywood advocate for artificial intelligence, though only for pre-production work.
cards.body:
Martin Scorsese has become an unexpected supporter of artificial intelligence in filmmaking, though with a specific limitation. The renowned director uses AI technology exclusively for storyboarding during pre-production, not for creating finished footage.

His public endorsement is significant in an industry where many creators have been skeptical of AI adoption. As one of the world's most famous living directors, Scorsese's position carries considerable weight and makes him among the first major Hollywood figures to openly advocate for AI tools in the filmmaking process.

cards.headline: Former Anduril engineer raises $42 million for composite parts manufacturing
cards.teaser: Layup Parts secured funding to streamline production of composite materials used in aerospace and automotive industries.
cards.body:
Layup Parts co-founder Zack Eakin raised $42 million to build a manufacturing platform for composite parts. Eakin previously worked for Palmer Luckey at Anduril and for Elon Musk, and drew on experience from motorsports to develop the company's approach.

The startup aims to produce composite materials faster and more affordably than current methods allow. Composites are used extensively in aerospace, automotive, and defense applications but often require lengthy custom manufacturing processes. Layup Parts positions itself as a marketplace that could standardize composite part production similar to how Amazon simplified retail distribution.

hero.headline: Liverpool great Kenny Dalglish undergoing cancer treatment
hero.body:
Kenny Dalglish, one of football's most celebrated figures, has confirmed he is undergoing treatment for cancer. The 75-year-old Scotland, Liverpool and Celtic legend made the announcement on Tuesday after accidentally posting about his treatment on social media earlier that day.

Dalglish revealed the news himself, saying: "As my inadvertent social media post has indicated, I am currently undergoing treatment for cancer. Unlike my mobile phone use, the treatment is going well." He expressed regret that the matter had become public, stating: "Ideally, this would have remained private because that's the way it should be, but my useless technology skills have forced my hand."

The former player and manager requested privacy for himself and his family as he continues his treatment. He also praised the medical staff involved in his care, saying: "Obviously I did not mean to make this matter public so I would appreciate it if the privacy of my family and myself are respected. As ever, thank you to the wonderful medical staff who have shown incredible care and discretion, not just for me but for many, many others. They are a credit to themselves."

Liverpool Football Club released a statement in response to the announcement, saying: "The support, best wishes and love of everyone at Liverpool FC are, and will be, with Sir Kenny and his family." The club also joined in requesting privacy during his treatment.

Dalglish enjoyed a legendary playing career at multiple clubs, beginning with Celtic before his famous move to Liverpool, where he became a central figure during the club's dominant era. He won numerous league titles and European trophies as a player and later managed Liverpool through significant periods, including the aftermath of the Hillsborough disaster in 1989, when he provided crucial support to affected families.

Beyond his time at Liverpool, Dalglish managed Blackburn Rovers, leading them to the Premier League title in 1995, and also managed Newcastle United. His contributions to football earned him a knighthood, recognizing both his sporting achievements and his broader impact on the game.

The announcement came on the same day that another Liverpool legend, John Barnes, revealed he had undergone prostate removal following a cancer diagnosis. Barnes said he is now "fine" and encouraged men to undergo testing and speak openly about such health issues, describing it as a taboo subject that needs greater awareness.

Dalglish remains widely considered Liverpool's greatest player and most revered figure at the club, respected not only for his outstanding talent as both player and manager but also for his character and leadership during the club's most challenging moments.

cards.headline: NFL star Myles Garrett joins Los Angeles Rams
cards.teaser: The Rams have announced defensive end Myles Garrett will wear number 95 for the team following his trade from Cleveland.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Rams acquired two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in a blockbuster trade. The 30-year-old edge rusher will wear number 95 for his new team.

In the deal, the Rams sent linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks to Cleveland. Garrett has been one of the league's elite defensive players since the Browns drafted him first overall in 2017. He set the single-season sacks record with 23 in 2025 and has accumulated 125.5 career sacks along with seven Pro Bowl selections.

cards.headline: Stephen Curry signs shoe deal with Chinese brand Li-Ning
cards.teaser: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has announced a new sneaker contract with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning.
cards.body:
Stephen Curry has signed a partnership with Li-Ning, the Chinese athletic apparel and footwear company. The deal marks a significant moment for the Chinese brand as it aims to expand its global presence in the competitive basketball shoe market.

The agreement comes after Curry ended his long-standing relationship with Under Armour in 2025. With one of basketball's biggest names now on its roster, Li-Ning has secured a major win in its efforts to compete with established international sneaker brands.

cards.headline: FIFA introduces new offside technology for 2026 World Cup
cards.teaser: Football's governing body has unveiled new offside detection technology that could reduce the use of delayed assistant referee flags.
cards.body:
FIFA has unveiled new offside technology set to debut at the 2026 World Cup. The innovation is designed to make offside decisions faster and more accurate during matches.

The technology could significantly reduce reliance on the delayed flag protocol, where assistant referees hold their flag to allow play to continue while the offside decision is reviewed. This practice has become standard in recent years but may become unnecessary with FIFA's new system.

cards.headline: Odell Beckham Jr. returns to New York Giants on minimum contract
cards.teaser: The wide receiver has signed a one-year deal to rejoin the Giants, where he began his NFL career.
cards.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. has signed with the New York Giants on a one-year minimum salary contract, reuniting with the franchise where he began his NFL career.

The Giants also added receivers JuJu Smith-Schuster and Braxton Berrios on similar one-year minimum deals as they work to upgrade their receiving group.

cards.headline: Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate nearing Real Madrid move
cards.teaser: The France international is in advanced negotiations to join the Spanish club on a free transfer after leaving Liverpool.
cards.body:
France defender Ibrahima Konate is in advanced talks with Real Madrid about joining the La Liga club on a free transfer following his departure from Liverpool.

The move would see the centre-back leave Anfield and move to the Spanish capital on a free transfer deal.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk reaches French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: Kostyuk became the first Ukrainian woman to reach the singles semifinals at Roland Garros, dedicating her victory to Ukraine.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk advanced to the French Open semifinals by defeating compatriot Elina Svitolina in an all-Ukrainian quarterfinal matchup. The victory marks a historic achievement for the Ukrainian player at one of tennis's premier events.

Kostyuk's win sends her into the last four of the tournament, where she will face Mirra Andreeva, who dominated Sorana Cirstea in her quarterfinal match.

hero.headline: Kennedy Center's National Symphony Orchestra Faces Existential Threat Amid Political Turmoil
hero.body:
The National Symphony Orchestra at the Kennedy Center is in serious jeopardy following a leadership overhaul initiated by President Trump after his second term began in early 2025. Musician Ben Folds warned that the orchestra's survival is now in question due to what he called the "callousness and confusion" surrounding the president's takeover of the institution.

The turmoil at the Kennedy Center has triggered widespread backlash from the arts community. Renowned composer Philip Glass, an 88-year-old Kennedy Center Honors recipient, withdrew the world premiere of his Symphony No. 15 "Lincoln" scheduled for June 12 and 13 in protest. Glass stated that the values of the Kennedy Center under its current leadership directly conflict with the message of his symphony, which portrays Abraham Lincoln. He felt obligated to withdraw the premiere.

Glass's decision reflects broader opposition from musical artists who oppose the administration's policies. The Kennedy Center has experienced a series of cancellations from performers voicing their concerns. In December, the Trump administration changed the venue's name to the "Trump-Kennedy Center," a move that intensified the backlash.

The administration has pursued what it describes as controversial changes to the institution's name and mission. Critics argue that the Trump administration's focus on what it considers "woke" or overly leftist culture politicizes the arts and alienates performers. Rhode Island senator Sheldon Whitehouse, an ex officio member of the Kennedy Center governing board, compared the situation to a takeover. "When the brigands took the ship, their first instinct was to loot it for their own benefit and hire their friends," he told the Guardian.

The National Symphony Orchestra has served as the Kennedy Center's resident orchestra since the venue opened in 1971. The ensemble performs classical concerts and provides the pit orchestra for performances at the venue. As a public-private partnership, the Kennedy Center relies on federal funding and private donations.

According to Folds, the workers at the Kennedy Center are the most harmed by the current situation, particularly the musicians of the National Symphony Orchestra. While he did not specify the exact operational or financial challenges the orchestra faces, he indicated that the ensemble's existence is now imperiled.

The crisis at the Kennedy Center occurs at a time when many performing arts institutions continue to struggle with financial pressures following pandemic-related disruptions. The National Symphony Orchestra, one of the nation's major orchestras, now faces an uncertain future under the new leadership at what has long been the nation's premier performing arts venue.

cards.headline: Netflix Developing Sequel to War Machine Following Streaming Success
cards.teaser: The military science fiction film starring Alan Ritchson has become one of Netflix's most-watched titles.
cards.body:
Netflix is moving forward with a sequel to War Machine, the science fiction action film that has drawn large viewership numbers on the streaming platform. Alan Ritchson starred in the original film as a staff sergeant who encounters a supernatural killing machine during a simulated military mission.

Director Patrick Hughes oversaw the first film. The sequel is currently in development, though no release date or production timeline has been announced.

cards.headline: Stop That Train Director Denies Film Used Artificial Intelligence
cards.teaser: Adam Shankman responded to social media claims about the RuPaul Charles movie's production methods.
cards.body:
Director Adam Shankman said the film Stop That Train, starring RuPaul Charles, was made entirely without generative artificial intelligence. He issued the statement after social media users claimed the production relied on AI technology.

Shankman wrote that every shot in the film was made by human hands. He said the movie contains zero AI elements, calling contrary claims patently not true.

cards.headline: Versant Media Invests in Microdrama Platform GammaTime
cards.teaser: The media company spun off from NBCUniversal is partnering with the short-form streaming service.
cards.body:
Versant Media participated in a Series A funding round for GammaTime, a streaming platform focused on microdramas. The investment establishes a partnership between the two companies. Versant owns MS NOW and CNBC and was separated from NBCUniversal earlier this year.

Under the agreement, GammaTime will work with Versant's properties.

cards.headline: Rapper Quando Rondo Moved to Halfway House After 15-Month Prison Term
cards.teaser: The Savannah rapper was released from prison after serving time on a marijuana charge.
cards.body:
Quando Rondo was transferred from prison to a halfway house after completing 15 months of incarceration. The rapper from Savannah, Georgia, had pleaded guilty to a marijuana charge in 2024.

A halfway house is a transitional facility where individuals complete the remainder of their sentences while preparing to reenter society. The arrangement typically allows residents to work or attend programs while remaining under supervision.

cards.headline: Chrissie Hynde Asks Concertgoers to Stop Using Cellphones
cards.teaser: The Pretenders singer wrote to fans requesting they put away their phones during performances.
cards.body:
Chrissie Hynde, lead singer of the Pretenders, has urged concert attendees to put away their cellphones during performances. In a letter to fans, she asked audiences to simply enjoy the show rather than recording or photographing it.

Hynde's appeal highlights a growing frustration among musicians about phone use at live events. She compared the behavior to something she finds objectionable, emphasizing her desire for fans to be fully present and engaged during concerts.

cards.headline: Fox Announces Summer Premiere Dates for Kitchen Nightmares and Beat Shazam
cards.teaser: Gordon Ramsay's restaurant show returns for a 10th season focused on Midwestern establishments.
cards.body:
Fox set premiere dates for its summer 2026 schedule, led by the return of Kitchen Nightmares on July 21. The 10th season of Gordon Ramsay's restaurant renovation show will debut with a two-hour episode at 8 p.m. and will feature struggling restaurants in the Midwest.

Ramsay will work with restaurant owners to revamp their operations. Additional summer programming dates were also announced, though specific shows and times were not detailed.

hero.headline: California governor primary results coming in as Porter, Steyer, Becerra compete
hero.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are competing against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
hero.body:
California voters are selecting Democratic nominees for governor in a primary election. The race features prominent candidates including Xavier Becerra, who is considered the establishment favorite, along with Katie Porter and Tom Steyer. Republican candidates Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are also competing.

The state uses a top-two primary system, so the two candidates receiving the most votes will advance to the general election regardless of party. The winner will replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who is not seeking reelection. As California's next governor will almost certainly be a Democrat, the primary outcome will determine what type of Democratic leadership the state receives.

cards.headline: Sanders to propose giving public 50 percent ownership of large AI companies
cards.teaser: Senator Bernie Sanders plans to introduce legislation that would grant the public a 50 percent stake in major artificial intelligence companies.
cards.body:
Sanders announced in a video message that he will introduce the AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act in the coming weeks. The Vermont independent said the bill would give the American public a 50 percent ownership stake in large AI companies.

The senator delivered his announcement in a nearly seven-minute video on the proposal. Sanders has been a vocal advocate for government intervention in technology and corporate sectors throughout his career in the Senate.

cards.headline: New York Democrats introduce measure to add four House seats through redistricting
cards.teaser: New York Democrats introduced a redistricting proposal that could add four congressional seats to their delegation in 2028 after an earlier redistricting effort failed.
cards.body:
Democratic legislators in New York introduced a measure on Monday that would reshape the state's congressional districts. The proposal uses a single constitutional amendment to remove barriers to mid-decade redistricting and allow changes to pass with a simple majority vote.

The effort follows Democrats' unsuccessful attempt to redraw voting districts earlier this year. If approved, the redistricting could add four seats to the Democratic congressional delegation starting in 2028.

cards.headline: Johnson tells Trump anti-weaponization fund unlikely to pass Congress
cards.teaser: Speaker Mike Johnson said he informed President Trump that a proposed anti-weaponization settlement fund faces difficult odds in Congress given tight Republican vote margins.
cards.body:
Speaker Mike Johnson told President Trump that his proposed "anti-weaponization" settlement fund would make it difficult for Republicans to advance critical legislation through Congress. Johnson cited narrow Republican vote margins in the House as the primary obstacle, indicating the fund lacks sufficient support within the GOP caucus.

Following their conversation, Johnson stated the fund is now "off the table." The Trump administration's Justice Department has disagreed strongly with a court ruling that halted the fund's establishment, though Johnson's comments suggest legislative obstacles have shifted the administration's focus elsewhere.

cards.headline: New Jersey sues immigration detention center operator over facility access
cards.teaser: The state filed a lawsuit seeking court-ordered access to inspect an immigration detention facility amid allegations of poor conditions and treatment.
cards.body:
New Jersey filed a lawsuit Tuesday against the private operator of Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Essex County Superior Court. The state is seeking court approval to allow the Department of Health to conduct inspections at the facility.

The legal action is based on allegations of unsanitary conditions and inadequate treatment of detainees. State officials argue they have been denied access to inspect the privately operated center.

cards.headline: New Mexico governor primary underway with Biden official Haaland in race
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland is competing against four other candidates in the primary to replace Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham.
cards.body:
New Mexico voters are selecting nominees for governor in a primary election. The race features Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, alongside Sam Bregman, Gregg Hull, Duke Rodriguez, and Doug Turner.

Haaland previously represented New Mexico in the U.S. House of Representatives before joining the Biden cabinet. The candidates are competing to replace Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham.

cards.headline: Nebraska releases cruise ship passengers from quarantine facility
cards.teaser: Five cruise ship passengers exposed to hantavirus were released from the National Quarantine Unit in Omaha.
cards.body:
Governor Jim Pillen welcomed the release of the five passengers from the facility on Tuesday. The Republican governor called the development positive and the product of partnership between the state, the University of Nebraska Medical Center, and federal health partners.

The passengers had been held at the National Quar
